title: MCP++ RevocationRecord@1
description: Signed, discoverable revocation of a UCAN/MCP++ delegation (Profile C). A verified RevocationRecord@1 makes the target delegation fail closed at execution time even when the original token signature remains cryptographically valid. Normative interface: RevocationRecord@1. Crypto: ADR-0002 Ed25519/EdDSA over mcpp-jcs-v1 canonical bytes. SwissKnife UCANRevocationRegistry is an observation source for field semantics (token CID, issuer, effective time, reason).
$comment: Interface label: RevocationRecord@1. Schema acceptance alone is not cryptographic conformance (ADR-0003). Validators must verify the signature and consult a durable ledger before admitting a revoked delegation.

issuer.description: DID of the principal that issued this revocation (typically the original delegation issuer or a designated revoker). Alias wire forms: iss, revoked_by, revokedBy.

revoked_delegation_cid.description: Content identifier of the revoked delegation token or proof bundle. Alias wire forms: token_cid, tokenCid, delegation_cid, cid (only when schema is absent and context is a bare SwissKnife entry).

effective_at.description: Unix epoch seconds (UTC) when the revocation becomes effective. Alias wire forms: effective_time, revoked_at, revokedAt (ISO-8601 strings are accepted by validators and normalized to epoch seconds).

replacement_cid.description: Optional CID of a replacement delegation that supersedes the revoked one. Alias: replacement.

signature.description: Detached Ed25519 signature (unpadded base64url, 64 raw bytes) over mcpp-jcs-v1 of the record body excluding signature metadata. Alias: sig.

alg.description: Signature algorithm. Downgrade to none/empty is forbidden.

kid.description: Key id of the verification key. Required when issuer is not a self-describing did:key.

public_key.description: Optional embedded Ed25519 public key (32 bytes, unpadded base64url or hex). Prefer did:key issuer resolution.

nonce.description: Optional unique nonce for this revocation record (replay resistance of the record itself).

cid.description: Optional content id of this RevocationRecord (CID of the signed body).

discovery.description: How verifiers locate this record. Required for discoverability claims; validators fail closed when a ledger is required but unavailable.

not_before.description: Optional earliest acceptance time for the record itself (alias: nbf).

expires_at.description: Optional record expiry. After expiry the revocation remains sticky for the target delegation once accepted by a durable ledger; new remote discovery MAY ignore expired transport envelopes.

delegationCid.description: Delegation or record content id. Accepts CIDv0 (Qm…), CIDv1 base32 (b…), and SwissKnife-style sha256:<hex> token digests.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch seconds (fractional allowed). Must be finite.

signature.description: Unpadded base64url Ed25519 signature (64 bytes → 86 chars) or hex (128 chars).

publicKey.description: 32-byte Ed25519 public key as unpadded base64url or 64-char hex.

discoveryMethod.description: Discovery channel for the record. ledger/registry are durable fail-closed stores; cid/bundle are content-addressed; gossip is best-effort transport; inline is embedded beside an invocation.

ledger_cid.description: CID of a durable revocation ledger snapshot containing this record.

registry_id.description: Logical id of a named revocation registry (SwissKnife-style singleton or kit ledger path key).

topic.description: Pubsub / gossip topic used to disseminate the record.

parents.description: Optional parent record CIDs for append-only discovery chains.

published_at.description: When the record was published for discovery (may differ from effective_at).

endpoint.description: Optional HTTPS or multiaddr endpoint that serves the record by CID.
